{{short description|American statistician and data scientist}}
{{about|the American statistician|the Canadian indie rock musician|Kathryn Calder|the New Zealand cross-country skier|Katie Calder}}
{{Use American English|date=February 2026}}
{{Use mdy dates|date=September 2025}}
'''Catherine A.''' "'''Kate'''" '''Calder''' is an American [[statistician]] who works as chair of Statistics and Data Sciences at the [[University of Texas at Austin]]. She was previously a professor of statistics at [[Ohio State University]]. Calder earned a bachelor's degree in mathematics from [[Northwestern University]] in 1999, and completed her Ph.D. in statistics from [[Duke University]] in 2003<ref name="cv">{{cite web |url=http://www.stat.osu.edu/~calder/CV_july15.pdf |title=Curriculum vitae |website=stat.osu.edu |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160616014040/http://www.stat.osu.edu/~calder/CV_july15.pdf |archive-date=June 16, 2016 |date=July 2015 |access-date=July 11, 2016}}</ref> under the joint supervision of David Higdon and Michael L. Lavine.<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=77453}}</ref> She joined the Ohio State faculty in 2003, and was promoted to full professor in 2015.<ref name="cv"/>

In 2013 she won the Young Investigator Award of the [[American Statistical Association]] (ASA),<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 13, 2013 |title=Kate Calder wins ASA Young Investigator Award |url=http://stat.duke.edu/news/kate-calder-wins-asa-young-investigator-award |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140228225258/http://stat.duke.edu/news/kate-calder-wins-asa-young-investigator-award <!-- or https://wayback.archive-it.org/all/20140228225258/http://stat.duke.edu/news/kate-calder-wins-asa-young-investigator-award --> |archive-date=2014-02-28 |publisher=Duke University Department of Statistical Science}}</ref> and in 2014 she was elected as a [[Fellow]] of the ASA "for outstanding contributions to the development of Bayesian statistical methodology for spatial and spatiotemporal data; for significant multidisciplinary collaborations; for excellence in teaching and mentoring graduate students both in statistics and in other disciplines; and for service to the profession."<ref>{{citation |url=https://www.amstat.org/newsroom/pressreleases/2014_ASAFellows.pdf |title=ASA Honors 63 New Fellows |publisher=[[American Statistical Association]] |date=June 11, 2014 |accessdate=July 11, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304054602/http://www.amstat.org/newsroom/pressreleases/2014_ASAFellows.pdf |archive-date=March 4, 2016 |url-status=dead}}.</ref> She was elected to the 2022 class of Fellows of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] (AAAS).<ref>{{Cite web |title=2022 AAAS Fellows |url=https://www.aaas.org/page/2022-fellows-0 |access-date=March 15, 2023 |website=American Association for the Advancement of Science (AAAS) |language=en}}</ref> In 2025 Calder was recipient of the [[American Statistical Association Founders Award|American Statistical Association's Founders Award]].<ref name=ASAFoundersAward>{{cite web | title=Founders Award | publisher=American Statistical Association | url=https://www.amstat.org/your-career/awards/founders-award }}</ref>
